title: Apply epic-d0d final-review findings (1 blocker, 3 should-fix, 4 nits)
description:
Final review returned REVISE. Apply exactly these 8 findings, nothing else:

1. BLOCKER — tk answer must not forge human gate verdicts (cmd/tk/cmd/answer.go): for PendingGate entries, enforce the same actor discipline as tk approve (resolveVerdictActor, cmd/tk/cmd/verdictguard.go): a runner-shaped actor is refused unless --from human attests a relayed human decision (add the flag to tk answer; it gains an entry in ResetFlags). Plain asks (PendingAsk) keep working without the flag. Tests: runner-shaped TK_ACTOR + tk answer approve on a gate → refused, gate intact; same with --from human → cleared with human stamp; PendingAsk unaffected.
2. Timeout keeps the question answerable (cmd/tk/cmd/ask.go askGiveUp): on --timeout do NOT resolve the entry — leave it unresolved (matching --collect --wait semantics), edit the message to say the run stopped waiting but the question remains open, exit with the timeout code. A later tk answer or a later run's consumer must be able to resolve it — test that exact sequence (timeout, then tk answer resolves and applies). Update the exit-5 stderr text, --help, and docs/operator-channel.md to the now-true contract.
3. Atomic first-resolution-wins (internal/operator/pending.go Resolve): take the existing .apply.lock around load-check-save so concurrent resolvers cannot overwrite each other; second resolver gets ErrAlreadyResolved (or the existing outcome). Concurrency test: two racing Resolve calls, exactly one wins, the loser's outcome is not applied and the message edit reflects the winner.
4. Multi-question ticks (internal/operator/engine.go Apply): clear the tick's awaiting only when no other OPEN (unresolved) pending entries reference the same tick; otherwise leave awaiting in place and do not cancel sibling questions as out-of-band. Test: two questions on one tick, answer one → sibling still open and answerable, awaiting still set; answer second → awaiting cleared.
5. Distinct timeout exit code: give timeout its own unused code (pick the next free one in root.go, likely 7), update the misleading ExitTimeout comment, ask/answer/collect paths, tests, and docs exit-code table. Verify no existing consumer of exit 5 semantics in the repo/tests breaks.
6. Note timestamps use res.AnsweredAt (internal/operator/engine.go noteLine), not apply-time now(); test a drain-later apply carries the decision time.
7. tk tell: empty text (args and stdin both empty/whitespace) → usage error, no HTTP.
8. Provenance honesty: stamp the resolution with the EVENT sender id (the actual telegram user) rather than the configured bound id (engine + telegram Adopt path); with the transport filter intact behavior is identical — add the test asserting the stamped id comes from the event.

Run: go test -short -count=1 ./internal/operator/... ./cmd/tk/... plus -race on internal/operator; gofmt clean; update docs/operator-channel.md wherever contracts changed (exit codes, timeout semantics).
